coverage_note: Whole file read in order. Latin-transliterated stretches (transcriber Latin, q for k): 06:05-13:00 partial, 18:14-24:11, 48:51-56:04, 57:52-1:05:45. Not filed (S4 pronunciation): ما تفي for مطفي (02:04), عطلوا for قاتلوا (26:47, dropped ق), كسا for كسر (27:52/28:13), اقرب for أغلب (17:38), شهر for شعر (44:12, she did call it out as 'month'), maqsudin for maksooreen (19:12), هلات إلى 12 for talaat illa tult (05:05, chat has it), بوتنا for 5u66atna (41:58), Asmaa vowel length (1:03:08). Self-fixes not filed: الأمبارح->امبارح (05:52/06:01), كان في محل->كنت (03:17), 'خروف is pig'->lamb (04:00, English meta), كسروا->انكسروا (14:57/15:06), اكسرو->ما تكسرو (17:13), meeting->ijtema (24:11), شعرها->شعرك (44:12/44:18), sawarti->sawarit (55:46). Not errors: asawi (08:27) and بوتك (38:27) are on her sheet (Sawwi / Boat). Unclear garbles left out: يومي امني (01:17), بتيت (01:24, she said 'it doesn't go' but the word is unrecoverable), شو كما ما مرا (01:58), آه هلا قلبك (04:42), haketni bare (10:48), kamamana (52:30/54:23). Ambiguous: 16:18 بتكسري vs her تكسري (chat has btekser) not filed. Speaker labels looked consistent; chat lines lag 30-120 s as expected.

rows.medi_said: معروف is ground؟ معروف؟ No. ... مرفوف؟ What was it؟ What was ground؟
rows.why: He reached for 'ground' and produced معروف (known) then the non-word مرفوف, gave up and asked; she supplied مفروم. Sheet: 'ground beef | La7meh mafrumeh | لحمة مفرومة'.
لحم is masculine; his second try made the adjective feminine (مفرومة) and she recast it to مفروم.
خضرا is feminine so the adjective should be مختلفة; he wavered and settled on masculine مختلف, she moved on (my reading, no signal).
Clock time needs el-saa3a (her sheet: 'at 2:00 | 3ala elsaa3a tentain'); she only corrected that he answered the wrong question (where, not when), so the time form was let pass (my reading).

rows.amal_said: Yeah, we don't say that yesterday. Just yesterday is its own...

rows.medi_said: Uh, Kevin, um, ami. Ami? Amoy?
rows.why: Building 'ibn 3ammi' he was unsure of the form (ami? amoy?) and she supplied عمي; more a hesitation than a wrong word.
Past 'he came' is aja; he said aji (I come / present shape) and she recast to أجا, which he repeated.
'Came to my house' takes 3ala (or 3andi); he used min (from) and she said no, أجا على, later أجا عندي.

rows.medi_said: Yeah. Aja andi wu rah bad, um, metakhri.
rows.why: He meant 'he left / went home late'; راح is 'went (somewhere)', the word for leaving/going home is روّح, which she supplied ('the better word would be بروح'). Sheet: 'i go home | Ana barawwe7 | أنا بروح'.

rows.medi_said: Uh, but fatad means, like, you choose?

rows.why: He did not recognise her بتفضل and asked if it meant 'you choose'; she re-taught بفضل and typed it. Sheet: 'i prefer | Ana bafaddel | أنا بفضل'.

rows.chat: e7na benfaddel enno inti ma tekserih

rows.chat: e7na benfaddel enno inti ma tekserih
rows.why: 'Break IT' needs the object ending; he stopped at ما تكسري and her typed line adds -ih.
For 'I broke it' the transcriber heard -u (كسرتوا, you-pl broke) twice while she said kasarto; she recast twice and typed KAsarto. May be only a vowel/pronunciation slip.

rows.amal_said: طيب. What about she broke it?
rows.why: 'He broke it' is kasaro (-o object); his form reads as كسروا 'they broke'. She said طيب by voice but typed kasaro.
'Why did THEY break them' needs the plural -u before the object (kasaruhom); he used the he-form كسرهم. She let it pass by voice and fixed it in chat.
He first said شو كسرهم, then talked himself into the get-broken form انكسر with an object; she recast كسرهم and he acknowledged ('It's inflicting').
'Since when' is min aimta; he said امتى alone, she said Perfect by voice, her chat line carries the min.

rows.amal_said: تكسري. What's plural of أشي إشي؟ ... تكسري أشياء.
rows.why: 'Things' is plural أشياء; he used singular شي, she asked for the plural and supplied it.
snen = years; teeth is snan. She pointed out he had said 'her years' and he corrected to snanha. Sheet: 'tooth brush | Furshayet snan | فرشاية سنان'.

rows.medi_said: Is qasa-- Did you-- Did we learn? That's just general, right? Cups is cups. Qasa.
rows.amal_said: Kasar? What's the... If we didn't learn it, then it's at.
rows.why: He did not know the plural of كاسة and asked; she gave the -at rule and he said qasat. Sheet: 'cup | Kaasa | كاسة'.
He blended كسر into the plural of كاسة and produced the non-word qasarat; she recast kasat and he took it. Sheet: 'cup | Kaasa | كاسة'.

'One OF the kids' needs من; he had none, she prompted with 'of', he added من.

'My mind/opinion' needs the -i ending; he said bare راي twice and she recast رأيي.
